clue.text: Killing the upsurge of revolutionary spirit

indicators.note: in a down entry an upsurge sends the whole run of letters climbing, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: red is the colour and byword of revolutionaries
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A violent death follows a sudden rise in revolutionary fervour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsurge of' turns the whole of REDRUM, giving the answer; both pieces flip together.
explanation.definitionFit: Murder is the unlawful deliberate killing of a person, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Encounter reserve in one's social network

parts.note: to face someone is to meet or encounter them
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Meeting someone kept back within your own circle of contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Facebook is the best-known social networking website, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Macbeth, for example, goes after final piece of fuel

indicators.note: the Scottish lord's title is placed after the single letter
the final letter of the word piece is taken

parts.note: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and Cawdor, a Scottish noble title

explanation.surface: Macbeth seems to be chasing the last bit of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final piece of fuel' looks like the last letter of fuel, but 'of' is a link: the final letter of 'piece' is taken and 'fuel' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas and burnt as a fuel.

clue.text: Not a pleasant walk pirates ordered

indicators.note: the letters of the word are put in a new order, as if ordered about

explanation.surface: Pirates were made to undertake an unpleasant march.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge wearily or reluctantly, a walk nobody enjoys.

clue.text: A fabric that is woven as and when pleases

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs, such as denim

explanation.surface: A woven cloth is made whenever one feels like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at will means doing it whenever one chooses, matching the idea of pleasing oneself.

definitions.meaning: The formal style used when addressing a Roman Catholic cardinal

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: prominence or distinction, and the honorific title by which cardinals are formally addressed.

clue.text: Junior officer makes warship change direction

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a naval fighting vessel
to alter something is to change it
N stands for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A junior officer orders a warship to turn about.
explanation.definitionFit: A subaltern is a British army officer below the rank of captain, hence junior.

definitions.meaning: to baffle them with a question they cannot answer
in cricket the wicketkeeper ... a batsman by breaking the wicket while he is out of his ground

explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both baffling a person and the cricket dismissal made by the wicketkeeper.

clue.text: Stimulant for a Northern Ireland development

indicators.note: a development is a working out into new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something exciting is said to be in store for the Northern Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Ireland' looks like the abbreviation NI, but only 'Northern' is cut to N; A, N and IRELAND are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone that stimulates the body in moments of stress or excitement.

definitions.meaning: a pride is the collective noun for a group of big cats living together
the British and Irish ... is the touring rugby union team drawn from Britain and Ireland

explanation.definitionFit: A pride is made up of these big cats, and the touring rugby team bears the same name.

parts.note: burn is the Scottish word for a stream, so a minor one is a tiny brook rather than a small injury

explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a very small stream, so it is the least of watercourses.

indicators.note: rough handling knocks the letters out of their order

explanation.surface: Going over uneven ground leaves a deep track.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow channel, as is a rut worn in a track.

clue.text: Transport used in winter or spring passage

parts.note: to skip is to spring or hop lightly
a lane is a narrow passage or way

explanation.surface: A vehicle suited to winter or to a springtime route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season set beside winter, but it is the verb meaning jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski-plane is an aircraft fitted with skis to land on snow, hence a cold-season means of travel.

definitions.meaning: to back somebody up is to support them
an irritated person is said to have their back up, like an angry cat arching

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means supports, and the idiom of a raised back describes someone getting annoyed.

clue.text: One should get on with it

definitions.text: One should get on with it

parts.words: One should get on with it
parts.note: read as getting on in life, the clue describes the drive that helps a person rise in the world

explanation.definitionFit: Ambition is the strong desire for success, the quality that helps someone get ahead.

definitions.meaning: a ... car has had a previous owner
something put to use has been employed and found useful

explanation.definitionFit: The word means pre-owned and also describes something employed for a purpose.

definitions.meaning: the thick fat of a whale is rendered for oil

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for sobbing and the fatty layer stripped from whales.

parts.note: a beau is a fashionable man, a dandy
a match that ends level is a draw, or a tie

explanation.surface: A fashionable young man sketches attractive women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draws' suggests sketching; here it is a level result, TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Beauties are attractive people, especially lovely women, the plural matching the plural definition.

indicators.note: the words are set in a different order to make a new arrangement

explanation.definitionFit: Meadows are fields of grass, often kept for hay, so they are grassland.

clue.text: Antiquated, so allowed to be held in honour

indicators.note: the phrase places one set of letters inside the award

parts.note: the OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned is permitted to remain held in esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means out of date or no longer used, as is anything antiquated.

indicators.note: the musical letter is placed after the rearranged letters
punishing treatment knocks the letters about into a new order

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: Somebody left slow-witted after a series of brutal fights.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a boxer after brutal fights; 'punishing' is really the anagram signal, its rearrangement giving OBTUS, and 'after' is a positional signal placing the note last.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone slow to understand, which is dull-witted.

clue.text: Irishman at church for spiritual guidance

parts.note: Sean is a typically Irish man's name
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: An Irishman goes to church to seek religious counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spiritual guidance' sounds religious but means contact with spirits of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which people seek messages from spirits, so it is guidance from the spirit world.

parts.note: read as a shared financial interest, it really means a pointed rod pushed through a roast of meat

explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pin used to hold meat together while cooking, a stake through a cut of meat.

clue.text: Make much of Tesco's new blend

indicators.note: a new blend mixes the letters into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Tesco is a large British supermarket chain; its possessive supplies the letters including the S

explanation.surface: Advertising a fresh mix of tea from a British supermarket.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or fuss over someone, which is making much of them.

definitions.meaning: the governing body of a country

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the governing political body and the verb means to declare or say.

clue.text: Bill is negative about raising it

indicators.note: the longer word goes about, or around, the shorter piece

parts.note: adverse means unfavourable or negative

indicators.note: in an across clue raising means the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A banknote is reluctant to see it brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a noun (a banknote or invoice) but is the verb to publicise; 'raising' turns the little word back to front, giving TI, before 'about' wraps the larger word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill a show is to announce or publicise it, the same as to promote it publicly.

parts.note: read not as a passenger ship but as the thing forming the edge or line along the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The coast is the land along the sea, the shoreline that borders an ocean.

indicators.note: the rearranged letters accept, or take in, the small word
somehow suggests the letters are jumbled in some unstated way

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone bitterly reluctant to take a little bung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' signals the anagram, giving STENER; 'accepting' then takes the little Scottish word inside. 'bribe' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for a bribe or inducement offered to sway someone.
